**Source file:** data/raw/crm_contacts.csv
**Data source name:** CRM_CONTACTS
**Entity type:** Person
**Generated by:** mapping_workflow

## Field Mappings

| Source Field | Senzing Attribute | Transformation | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| contact_id | RECORD_ID | verbatim | Stable natural key, 100% unique |
| (constant) | DATA_SOURCE | `CRM_CONTACTS` | Root attribute |
| (constant) | RECORD_TYPE | `PERSON` | Own feature object; individual customers, no organization records, no type field |
| full_name | NAME_FULL | verbatim | Single name field: not split |
| email | EMAIL_ADDRESS | verbatim | |
| phone | PHONE_NUMBER | verbatim | Three formats in the source; emitted as-is |
| address | ADDR_FULL | verbatim | Single free-text address: not split; Senzing parses it |
| created_date | payload `created_date` | verbatim | Two date formats in the source; not used for matching |

Blank values are omitted.

## Mapping Decisions

- One master schema (crm_contacts); no child, lookup or relationship schemas; no embedded second entity.
- NAME_FULL and ADDR_FULL because the source supplies one field for each (the mapping reference: a single string maps to the *_FULL form and is not split).
- Payload key `created_date` is not a registered feature attribute name.
- Cross-source collision check against WEB_ORDERS — all pairs exempt, recorded here:
  - NAME: full_name vs first_name + last_name — parsed vs full, both the record subject.
  - ADDRESS: address vs street/city/state/zip — parsed vs full, same subject, no usage type on either.
  - EMAIL: email vs email; PHONE: phone vs phone — same quantity on a feature-specific feature.

## Quality Notes

- Source quality score 93.4 (Strong). Output population equals source presence: NAME 100%, EMAIL 95.1%, ADDRESS 90.1%, PHONE 88.2%.
- sz_json_analyzer.py: no errors or warnings (4,000 records). sz_verbatim_check.py: all values verbatim (run on a CSV-to-JSONL copy; known tool limitation). sz_routing_report.py: only contact_id listed as dropped (it is RECORD_ID).
- ~300 records are second contacts for the same customer under distinct contact_ids; resolution, not the mapper, joins them.
- Structurally validated; semantic validation happens at Data processing's match-key audit.
